$description: product: move. Mizan Move — ride-booking, read at a curb in one glance, compact density. The same eighteen tokens as product.market and the same mechanism: action.primary and its hover name primitives because they depend on this dimension alone, and text.secondary selects the Move slot because its value depends on the theme too. Move's secondary text is the lighter step in both themes — neutral.650 in light, neutral.500 in dark. That is decision 008's most consequential refusal made structural: the audit named merging Market's and Move's secondary text the most damaging cleanup available, and this file is where the refusal is enforced in every combination rather than only in the one somebody happened to screenshot. It shows up in the numbers as the tightest neutral text pairing in the system — text.secondary on surface.sunken at 4.76:1 in light+move, against a 4.5 bar, and the tightest of any kind until decision 023 added text.error at 4.73:1 on the same ground in dark. The control block is where 'compact' stops being a word and gets tested, and it fails the word: SIX of the fifteen values here are LARGER than Market's, not smaller. Decision 022 has the measurements and decision 020 found them. Move's md is Move's only real button — v0's .mv-action, 53.5px, which lands on Market's lg — because Move is compact in what it puts on a screen and generous in the one thing a thumb has to find at a curb. Move's sm is identical to Market's, stated rather than omitted, because a step whose definition is a WCAG exemption does not vary with a product's mood. Move's lg is the one block in this file with no v0 evidence behind it at all; it is one rung above Move's md by construction, and 022 says so.
